description: A purple hook with one pale ridge of light down the curve, and a hard green crust dried on the last third of the point.
lore: Tip the bag out after a night's work on the eastern ground and most of it is other creatures' property — hooks off a big cat, shed talons, a wet eye with somebody else's iris in it. That is why a heap of leavings usually settles nothing: the details are real but they are the wrong creature's details, and details are the whole reason anyone stoops. This hook is the exception on the cloth. It grew where it sits, it is sized to the hand it grew on, and everything else in the bag gets carried home on its credit.

In the hand it is longer than a finger and curved well past any use. A pale ridge of light runs down the outer edge where the wear is, the purple goes almost black at the base, and the base is a socket rather than a tang, shaped round a knuckle that is not there any more, with nothing on it to haft. People try. It makes a poor knife every time and they keep the poor knife, because a claw is worth nothing and a claw with a hand behind it is worth something, and that difference is the whole reason anyone stoops for one.

The last third of the point is crusted, mustard at the base of the crust and hard green at the tip, sitting on the purple rather than in it, so it was put there and did not grow there. It flakes under a thumbnail, and a kept one travels point-down in a stiff wrap by people who wash afterwards. That green is not unique to this creature: the stitched-together thing further along the black rock leaks the same colour, and two unrelated heaps off the same ground agreeing about a pigment is exactly the sort of coincidence a heap of leavings exists to catch. Which way it ran is not readable. A crusted point has either delivered that green into something or taken it out of something, and the crust will not say. The bag does not answer the question. It carries it.
